data.narrative:
Dexterity, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Samir Menon and others, carries a current post-money valuation of $1.65B on $291M total raised. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics firms plus one public comparable, with five primary peers spanning Series B and Series C stages: Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), Agile Robots ($1.0B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage advancement against the $1.6B last post-money valuation, yielding $3.1B. Peer-median analysis across the five same-sector comparables produces a median of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer set reflects modest dispersion, suggesting valuation stability at the current stage.

The two methods produce a triangulated range of $1.4B (low) to $3.6B (high), with a median estimate of $2.4B. The $1.65B current valuation sits near the lower quartile of this range. Key uncertainties include execution risk on Series B capital deployment, relative technology differentiation versus the five direct peers, and market timing for Series C fundraising—factors that could justify either compression toward the peer median or expansion toward stage-progression upside.
